newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee stays weak on dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee stays weak on dollar demand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed at the top end of the Central Bank range due to commercial demand for dollars, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.15 to the dollar after opening at its previous closing level of 57.14, they said.
"Despite a big seller of dollars and the only direction left for the exchange rate being down, the currency was maintained near the top by genuine demand," said an ABN Amro Bank dealer.
There was sufficient import covering demand to restrict the downside to about 57.13, despite selling by a big non-banking institution, dealers said.
The Central Bank buying and selling prices were unchanged at 56.0241 and 57.1559.
Overnight call money closed at its opening level of 15.5 percent, despite two big state borrowers in the market, dealers said.
"Since the money market was very liquid there was no impact either from big borrowing or from banks covering imports with dollars bought from the Central Bank," said a Hatton National Bank dealer.
